title: Design Front Middle Back Queue
description:
Design a queue supporting `O(1)` insertions and removals at the **front**, **middle**, and **back**.

Implement the `FrontMiddleBackQueue` class:
- `FrontMiddleBackQueue()` initializes an empty queue.
- `void pushFront(int val)` adds `val` to the front of the queue.
- `void pushMiddle(int val)` inserts `val` at 0-based index `floor(n / 2)` where `n` is the current size.
- `void pushBack(int val)` adds `val` to the back of the queue.
- `int popFront()` removes and returns the front element, or `-1` if empty.
- `int popMiddle()` removes and returns the element at 0-based index `floor((n - 1) / 2)` (the frontmost of the two middle elements when `n` is even), or `-1` if empty.
- `int popBack()` removes and returns the back element, or `-1` if empty.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made across all operations.
hints: Split the elements across two doubly linked lists (deques) `left` and `right`, maintaining the invariant `left.size == right.size` or `left.size == right.size + 1`.
Under this invariant, `popMiddle` always pops the back of `left`, and `pushMiddle` moves the back of `left` to the front of `right` if `left.size > right.size` before appending to `left`.

examples.explanation: Pushes form [1, 4, 3, 2]; pops remove front 1, middle 3, middle 4, back 2, then empty -1.
Popping from an empty queue always returns -1; pushing to middle on empty inserts at index 0.
Alternating pushFront, pushMiddle, and pushBack maintains exact middle indices for both even and odd sizes.
